text.en:
Asha had one warm roti. Her friend Kabir came to play.
Asha tore the roti into two pieces that were exactly the same size. "One for you, one for me," she said.
Later her cousins came too. Asha and Kabir tore each piece again, so there were four equal pieces for four children.
How much of the roti did each child get?

A whole can be shared into equal parts.
Share a whole into 2 equal parts: each part is one half.
Share a whole into 4 equal parts: each part is one quarter.
The parts must be exactly equal. If one part is bigger, it is not a half.
2 halves make 1 whole. 4 quarters make 1 whole. 2 quarters make 1 half.
Imagine a chapati. Fold it so both sides match exactly. Now you have two equal parts.
Each part is one half. Two halves put together make one whole chapati.
Fold it once more. Now there are four equal parts. Each one is a quarter.
Two quarters make a half. Four quarters make a whole. Remember: the parts must always be equal.

problem.en: A pizza is cut into 4 equal slices. Ravi eats 1 slice. How much of the pizza has he eaten, and how much is left?

text.en: Count the equal slices. There are 4, so each slice is one quarter.
Ravi ate 1 slice, so he ate one quarter of the pizza.

why.en: He took 1 of the 4 equal parts.

text.en: Slices left: 4 take away 1 is 3 slices. Three quarters are left.

why.en: What is left is the other 3 equal parts.

prompt.en: A friend says "a half is the bigger piece when you break a roti." What would you tell your friend?

requiredIdeas.en: A half is one of TWO EQUAL parts.
If the two parts are not equal, neither part is a half.

commonMisconceptions.en: Calling any piece a half, even when the pieces are not equal.

points.en: A half is one of 2 equal parts. A quarter is one of 4 equal parts.
2 halves make a whole. 4 quarters make a whole. 2 quarters make a half.
